## The Purpose of Tests {.passage-heading}

```{=html}
<div class="note-row passage-row" data-p="53"><div class="note-main"><div class="note-head"><a class="note-num" href="../read.html#p53" title="Paragraph 53 in the full text">53</a></div><div class="note-text">Know verily that the purpose underlying all these symbolic terms and abstruse allusions, which emanate from the Revealers of God’s holy Cause, hath been to test and prove the peoples of the world; that thereby the earth of the pure and illuminated hearts may be known from the perishable and barren soil. From time immemorial such hath been the way of God amidst His creatures, and to this testify the records of the sacred books.</div></div><aside class="note-side"><textarea class="note-input" rows="2" aria-label="Your note on paragraph 53" placeholder="Your note on paragraph 53…"></textarea><div class="note-bar"><span class="note-saved"></span></div></aside></div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="note-row passage-row" data-p="54"><div class="note-main"><div class="note-head"><a class="note-num" href="../read.html#p54" title="Paragraph 54 in the full text">54</a></div><div class="note-text">Verily, God caused not this turmoil but to test and prove His servants. Otherwise, He, the ideal King, could easily have left the Qiblih unchanged</div></div><aside class="note-side"><textarea class="note-input" rows="2" aria-label="Your note on paragraph 54" placeholder="Your note on paragraph 54…"></textarea><div class="note-bar"><span class="note-saved"></span></div></aside></div>
<div class="note-row passage-row" data-p="55"><div class="note-main"><div class="note-head"><a class="note-num" href="../read.html#p55" title="Paragraph 55 in the full text">55</a></div><div class="note-text">Notwithstanding the truth of these facts, why should the Qiblih have been changed, thus casting such dismay amongst the people, causing the companions of the Prophet to waver, and throwing so great a confusion into their midst? Yea, such things as throw consternation into the hearts of all men come to pass only that each soul may be tested by the touchstone of God, that the true may be known and distinguished from the false.</div></div><aside class="note-side"><textarea class="note-input" rows="2" aria-label="Your note on paragraph 55" placeholder="Your note on paragraph 55…"></textarea><div class="note-bar"><span class="note-saved"></span></div></aside></div>
<div class="note-row passage-row" data-p="56"><div class="note-main"><div class="note-head"><a class="note-num" href="../read.html#p56" title="Paragraph 56 in the full text">56</a></div><div class="note-text">Such things take place only that the souls of men may develop and be delivered from the prison-cage of self and desire. Otherwise, that ideal King hath, throughout eternity, been in His Essence independent of the comprehension of all beings, and will continue, forever, in His own Being to be exalted above the adoration of every soul.</div></div><aside class="note-side"><textarea class="note-input" rows="2" aria-label="Your note on paragraph 56" placeholder="Your note on paragraph 56…"></textarea><div class="note-bar"><span class="note-saved"></span></div></aside></div>
```

::: {.passage-body}
1. Bahá'u'lláh says that the purpose of the Prophets in using symbolic language and the unexpected events that occur during their lives are both to test and prove us and also so that our souls can develop. A test is a procedure or trial used to measure knowledge, quality, ability, or the presence of a substance. In what sense do tests help us to develop? It may be helpful to reflect on the use of the word *test* in the following examples. What is the meaning of *test* in each case?
:::

```{=html}
<div class="denial-list">
<figure class="denial"><blockquote><p>"O Son of Being! Busy not thyself with this world, for with fire We test the gold, and with gold We test Our servants."</p></blockquote><figcaption><span class="denial-prophet">Bahá'u'lláh</span><span class="denial-source">The Hidden Words, Arabic 55</span></figcaption></figure>
<figure class="denial"><blockquote><p>"These tests, even as thou didst write, do but cleanse the spotting of self from off the mirror of the heart, till the Sun of Truth can cast its rays thereon; for there is no veil more obstructive than the self, and however tenuous that veil may be, at the last it will completely shut a person out, and deprive him of his portion of eternal grace."</p></blockquote><figcaption><span class="denial-prophet">ʻAbdu'l‑Bahá</span><span class="denial-source">Selections from the Writings of ʻAbdu'l‑Bahá</span></figcaption></figure>
<figure class="denial"><blockquote><p>"O my heavenly friends! It is certain and evident that the Incomparable One is always praised for His absolute wealth, distinguished for His all-embracing mercy, characterized by His eternal grace, and known for His gifts to the world of existence. Nonetheless, in accordance with His inscrutable wisdom and in order to apply a unique test to distinguish the friend from the stranger, He hath enjoined the Ḥuqúq upon His servants and made it obligatory."</p></blockquote><figcaption><span class="denial-prophet">Bahá'u'lláh</span><span class="denial-source">Ḥuqúqu'lláh</span></figcaption></figure>
</div>
```


::: {.passage-body}
2. In relation to this, Bahá'u'lláh states that 'the ways of the Manifestations of God' are 'contrary' 'to the ways and desires of men' ([¶61](../read.qmd#p61)). He then gives examples of events in the lives of previous Prophets which were contrary to the ways and desires of the people of their day and became a test for them. For Moses it was the accusation of murder ([¶57](../read.qmd#p57), [¶58](../read.qmd#p58)), for Jesus it was the fatherless birth ([¶59](../read.qmd#p59), [¶60](../read.qmd#p60)), and for Muḥammad it was the changing of the Qiblih ([¶54](../read.qmd#p54), [¶55](../read.qmd#p55)). What about for the current day? What things has Bahá'u'lláh said or done that are contrary to our ways and desires? How might these tests help our souls to grow and develop?
:::

## The Meaning of Symbolic Terms Used by the Prophets (Continued) {.passage-heading}

::: {.passage-body}
In these paragraphs Bahá'u'lláh has given symbolic interpretations to terms that are commonly used by the Prophets of old. Here is a summary of the terms He has explained so far:

- **Earth** — human hearts
    - Paragraphs [48](../read.qmd#p48), [49](../read.qmd#p49), [51](../read.qmd#p51)
- **Heaven** — divine revelation
    - Paragraphs [46](../read.qmd#p46), [51](../read.qmd#p51), [52](../read.qmd#p52)
- **Oppression** — truth being obscured; corruption of foolish and ignorant leaders
    - Paragraphs [28](../read.qmd#p28), [29](../read.qmd#p29), [30](../read.qmd#p30)
- **Sun, Moon, Stars** — Manifestations of God and their followers; religious leaders of the former dispensation; teachings and laws of the former dispensation
    - Paragraphs [31](../read.qmd#p31), [34](../read.qmd#p34), [38](../read.qmd#p38), [41](../read.qmd#p41)

3. Shoghi Effendi claims that if we ponder on the Book of Certitude we 'will obtain a clear insight into the old scriptures'. Let us now turn to some of these scriptures and see if we can understand them in light of what we have learned.
:::

::: {.passage-body}
4. In addition to these more explicit interpretations, some scholars have observed that Bahá'u'lláh also implicitly interprets many other terms in these paragraphs through the use of a construct called a *genitive metaphor*. This is a metaphor that is built using a possessive or descriptive construction, for example 'a flood of messages'. One noun is the actual subject (messages) and the other is a figurative image (flood). Bahá'u'lláh uses this device to aid His interpretations. He explains a symbolic term which was previously unclear by suggesting its referent.<sup class="src-ref" role="button" tabindex="0" data-note-head="Source" data-note="Christopher Buck, Symbol and Secret: Qur’án Commentary in Bahá’u’lláh’s Kitáb-i-Íqán." data-note-href="https://bahai-library.com/buck_symbol_secret_quran" aria-label="Source note">†</sup> For example, take the explanation of the changing of the earth:

    > In like manner, endeavor to comprehend the meaning of the "changing of the earth." Know thou, that upon whatever hearts the bountiful showers of mercy, raining from the "heaven" of divine Revelation, have fallen, the earth of those hearts hath verily been changed into the earth of divine knowledge and wisdom. What myrtles of unity hath the soil of their hearts produced! What blossoms of true knowledge and wisdom hath their illumined bosoms yielded! … Methinks they have been molded from the clay of infinite knowledge, and kneaded with the water of divine wisdom … Thus hath He said: "On the day when the earth shall be changed into another earth."
    >
    > [Bahá'u'lláh, *Kitáb-i-Íqán* [¶48](../read.qmd#p48)]{.attrib}

    Which images can you find working this way in this week's paragraphs, and what does each one interpret?
:::

::: {.passage-body}
